title: Etale coordinates preserve the normalized section deformation comparison
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $S,V$ be Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $g:V\to S$ be smooth separated of finite type and pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $s:S\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed section that is regular of codimension $d$: its ideal $\mathcal I$ is locally generated by $d$ elements, each a nonzerodivisor modulo its predecessors. Put $N=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2)$ with projection $\pi$ and zero section $z$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section, lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]. Suppose $U\subset V$ is an open neighbourhood of $s(S)$ and $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_S$ is a separated etale finite-type $S$-morphism with $e\circ s=0$ and $e^{-1}(0)=s(S)$ scheme-theoretically [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. Write $q:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ for the projection. The classes of $e^*x_1,\ldots,e^*x_d$ give the specified frame of $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ and the associated normal-bundle isomorphism $\lambda:N\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf A^d_S$.

Use the whole ordinary etale derived categories of constant $A$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For every indicated smooth map $h$, put $\omega_h=h^\times A$ using the compact-support right adjoint [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Assume the smooth maps and deformation maps in this paragraph are compactifiable [def-asd-compactifiable]. Let $\delta_{g,s}:s^*\omega_g\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*\omega_\pi$ be the normalized comparison of [lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization], using the actual extended-Rees deformation $\operatorname{Spec}_V\mathcal O_V[t,\mathcal I/t]$ and its canonical zero-fibre identification, sending $a/t^j\bmod t$ to the degree-$j$ class of $a$. Let $\chi_e:s^*\omega_g\xrightarrow{\sim}0^*\omega_q$ be restriction of the counit-preserving etale locality comparison $\omega_g|_U\simeq e^*\omega_q$ of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], and let $\chi_\lambda:z^*\omega_\pi\xrightarrow{\sim}0^*\omega_q$ be the corresponding comparison for $\lambda$. Then the actual maps satisfy
$$\chi_\lambda\circ\delta_{g,s}=\chi_e.$$
The comparisons use the normal frame induced by the ideal classes, rather than an arbitrary bundle trivialization. No Tate orientation is selected in this assertion.

source.place: Local construction: etale maps of pairs, deformed coordinates x_i=t u_i, and normalization at t=1; ordinary Noetherian section-invariant interface of lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization

proof.text: Put $T=\mathbf A^1_S$, $a:T\to S$, $D=\operatorname{Def}_s(V)$, $C=s^*\omega_g$ and $F=\widetilde s^*\omega_{\widetilde g}$. The section-specialization theorem supplies the actual smooth deformation, the fibre identifications $\theta_1:i_1^*F\simeq C$, $\theta_0:i_0^*F\simeq C_N:=z^*\omega_\pi$, and the uniquely normalized $\kappa:F\simeq a^*C$. In these notations $\delta=\theta_0(i_0^*\kappa)^{-1}$. Keep the fibre identifications in the formulas, rather than suppressing them. Also put $Q:\mathbf A^d_T\to T$, $r:\mathbf A^d_T\to\mathbf A^d_S$, $o:S\to\mathbf A^d_S$, $o_T:T\to\mathbf A^d_T$, and $C_q=o^*\omega_q$. The square $(Q,r,a,q)$ is Cartesian. Both affine projections are smooth of pure dimension $d$.

source.place: Opening paragraph: family and canonical fibre identifications; Local construction: affine-space family

proof.text:
Write $D_U=D\times_VU$. On affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset U$ mapping into $\mathbf A^d_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$ put $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$ and $I=JB$. The equality $I=JB$ is precisely the scheme-theoretic centre hypothesis. Since $e$ is etale it is flat; the affine flatness criterion says $B$ is a flat $P$-module. Tensoring $J^m\hookrightarrow P$ with $B$ identifies $B\otimes_PJ^m$ with $I^m$. The Laurent pieces of $P[t,J/t]$ are $Pt^k$ for $k\geq0$ and $J^mt^{-m}$ for $m>0$. Tensoring their inclusions and multiplying coefficients therefore gives the canonical algebra isomorphism
$$B\otimes_PP[t,J/t]\simeq B[t,I/t].$$
The monomial correspondence $x^\alpha t^k\leftrightarrow u^\alpha t^{k+|\alpha|}$, for $k\geq-|\alpha|$, identifies $P[t,J/t]$ with $R[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$, with $x_j=tu_j$. All maps are the identity on $B,t$ and send $u_j$ to $e^*x_j/t$, so they agree on overlaps. Thus globally $D_U=U\times_{\mathbf A^d_S}\mathbf A^d_T$, where the second map is $(u,t)\mapsto tu$.

source.place: Local construction, first paragraph, x_i=t u_i; Stacks 01U5/lemma-flat-characterize and 00HD/lemma-flat

proof.text: The second projection $E:D_U\to\mathbf A^d_T$ is separated etale of finite type: it is the base change of $e$. It carries $\widetilde s$ to $o_T$. At $t=1$ the preceding ring map is $x_j\mapsto u_j$, hence $E_1=e$. At $t=0$ it is $u_j\mapsto[e^*x_j]\in I/I^2$. Under the canonical zero-fibre identification fixed in the statement this is exactly $E_0=\lambda$, not its composite with an arbitrary linear automorphism. Indeed $e^*x_j/t\bmod t$ goes to the degree-one ideal class, and products give the stated map in every degree. This uses the conormal algebra's specified degree-one map and the normal-fibre identification supplied by the section-specialization theorem. The open $D_U\subset D$ contains the entire deformed section, since its image in $V$ is $s(S)$.

source.place: Local construction: etale map of pairs; canonical deformed coordinates and the two fibres

proof.text: All locality and exchange maps used below are on the whole ordinary unbounded etale derived categories with the same finite constant ring $A$. Here are their geometric hypotheses. The schemes $T,\mathbf A^d_S,\mathbf A^d_T$ are Noetherian by finite type over a Noetherian base, and $D$ is Noetherian by the section-specialization theorem. Their open subschemes $U,D_U$ are Noetherian. The inclusions $j:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $J:D_U\hookrightarrow D$ are etale; they are separated, and finite type because opens of Noetherian schemes are quasi-compact and an open immersion is locally an isomorphism. The maps $e,E$ are separated finite-type etale by hypothesis and Step 3. The maps $q,Q,\pi,\widetilde g,g$ are compactifiable as assumed. For the restrictions $g|_U,\widetilde g|_{D_U}$, their diagonals are closed by restriction of the original diagonals, and they are finite type by composition. Every Noetherian target is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so Nagata also provides all auxiliary compactifications, including those of $j,J,e,E,\lambda$. Thus etale locality applies to every composite below; $\ell^n A=0$ and $\ell^n$ is invertible on every scheme concerned, as smooth exceptional base change requires. Restriction by the open etale maps preserves smoothness and pure relative dimension, by smooth relative-dimension permanence.

source.place: Local construction: hypotheses for ordinary etale locality and smooth exceptional base change

proof.text:
We use the following direct instance of the cited coherence statements. Write $L_{f,u}:u^*\omega_f\simeq\omega_{fu}$ for counit-preserving etale locality, and $b_f:v_X^*\omega_f\simeq\omega_{f'}$ for smooth exceptional base change along $v:B'\to B$. If $u:W\to X$ is one of the etale maps and $u':W'\to X'$ its base change, then
$$b_{fu}\circ v_W^*L_{f,u}=L_{f',u'}\circ u'^*b_f.$$
To check this identity, use the compact-support composition $Rf_!Ru_!\simeq R(fu)_!$. The exchange for this composite is, by compatibility with composition, the exchange for $u$ followed by that for $f$. The etale compact-support normalization identifies the first exchange with the sum-extension exchange, including its counit. Take mates of these two equal composites: mate-pasting along adjunctions, followed by change of adjunction by the normalization comparison, gives precisely the displayed equality. Here $L$ and $b$ are the mates specified in the locality and smooth-base-change statements. Likewise two successive changes of base give the composite $b$ by mate-pasting along the horizontal functors; an identity change gives the identity by the identity clause. This is a formal substitution into the cited equalities, with no purity or orientation assertion added.

source.place: Local construction and normalization: formal coherence of the canonical maps; Stacks 0E46/remark-compose-base-change and 0E47/remark-compose-base-change-horizontal

proof.text:
Restrict etale locality for $J:D_U\hookrightarrow D$ and $E:D_U\to\mathbf A^d_T$ to their common section. Since $\widetilde g|_{D_U}=QE$, this gives
$$\widetilde\chi:F\xrightarrow{\sim}o_T^*\omega_Q,$$
namely the section pullback of $L_{Q,E}^{-1}L_{\widetilde g,J}$. Smooth base change for $q$ along $a$ gives $b_{q,a}:r^*\omega_q\simeq\omega_Q$. Pulling this map to $o_T$ gives
$$\eta:a^*C_q\xrightarrow{\sim}o_T^*\omega_Q.$$
Define $H=\eta^{-1}\widetilde\chi:F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C_q$. These are actual adjunction comparisons. Inverse images are exact constant-coefficient inverse images, so their degreewise derived functors preserve these composites and inverses.

source.place: Local construction, second paragraph: compare the family and the original section to the same affine-space family

proof.text:
Apply Step 5 to $J$ and $E$ with the two changes of base $i_r:S\to T$, $r=0,1$. The fibre maps of $J$ are respectively $j:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $1_N$, since $U$ contains the whole centre; the fibre maps of $E$ are $e$ and $\lambda$ by Step 3. For $q$, the composite base change along $a i_r=1_S$ is the identity; hence the fibre comparison for $Q$ cancels $i_r^*\eta$. The locality square of Step 5, pulled to the sections, now reads explicitly
$$i_1^*H=\chi_e\theta_1,\qquad i_0^*H=\chi_\lambda\theta_0.$$
For example the second equality before cancellation is $b_{Q,i_0}\,i_0^*\widetilde\chi=\chi_\lambda\theta_0$ and $b_{Q,i_0}\,i_0^*\eta=1_{C_q}$, where $b_{Q,i_0}$ denotes its pullback to the zero section. At $1$ the same equations have $e,\theta_1$ in place of $\lambda,\theta_0$. Thus both fibre identities compare the specified maps, including their normalization.

source.place: Local construction: fibre at t=1, normal frame at t=0, and normalization

proof.text:
Set $K=(a^*\chi_e^{-1})H:F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C$. Step 7 gives $i_1^*K=\theta_1$, so uniqueness in the section-specialization theorem gives $K=\kappa$. At zero it gives
$$i_0^*\kappa=\chi_e^{-1}\chi_\lambda\theta_0.$$
Invert this equality and use Step 1's formula for $\delta$ to obtain $\delta=\chi_\lambda^{-1}\chi_e$, or $\chi_\lambda\delta=\chi_e$, as asserted. Empty $S$ causes no exception: every map is unique. For $d=0$ there are no coordinate generators, $e^{-1}(0)=U=s(S)$, and all the same formulas reduce to identities. The calculation used flatness over $R[x]$, never reducedness of $R$ or a global isomorphism $U\simeq\mathbf A^d_S$.
